relations.note: Ayots is one of the supreme creator Yato’ Yos’s sons.
Poporrona’ is explicitly Ayots’s son, whom he carries because he cannot walk.
Ayots names encountered beings in response to Poporrona’s questions, transforming them.
In the usual Asháninka genealogy, Avíreri is Kíri’s grandfather.
Avíreri carries Kíri, who prompts transformations, mourns him, and later becomes peach-palm.
Quërí is Mábireri’s young relative; the precise kin relationship varies.
Mábireri carries Quërí and transforms encountered people after the child questions him.
Armadillo is Ayots or Avíreri’s brother-in-law through his unnamed sister.

relations.myth: Armadillo seals Ayots in an underground house
relations.note: After Ayots transforms his children, Armadillo traps and permanently confines him underground.

relations.myth: Avíreri’s fall through the dancing-ground trap
relations.note: After falling into the trap, Avíreri transforms his frightened brother-in-law into armadillo.

relations.myth: Avíreri reaches Otsitiríko at River’s End
relations.note: Pachákama prevents Avíreri’s return, keeping him bound by a strangler vine.

relations.myth: Avíreri supports the earth at River’s End
relations.note: At Pachákama’s request, Avíreri remains at Otsitiríko helping support the earth.
Some Matsigenka usage reportedly treats Pachákama and the Avíreri-equivalent interchangeably.
The bird-being Ciraráto prevents Avíreri completing a dam intended to destroy the Asháninka.
Santos-Granero proposes Ayots and Avíreri as an inverted Indigenous transformation of Saint Christopher.
relations.source: Santos-Granero, Saint Christopher in the Amazon
